svg.title: Around the table
svg.desc: Original family-manga illustration: plate, related to Around the table.

text.tspan: To share a meal is to negotiate a familiar but frequently obscured relationship between intentional design and the contingencies of
shared experience. The question is not whether arrangements are desirable, but what authority they should acquire. A credible
position supports preparation while withholding the assumption that procedural coherence is equivalent to human value.
There is a substantive case for structure: a simple plan leaves time for conversation. Here, we prepare the vegetables before our guests arrive. The arrangement earns
its legitimacy through the specific difficulty it alleviates, not through its conformity to an abstract ideal of order. Its success is consequently conditional. Once the
intervention demands more attention than the obstacle it removes, the original justification begins to unravel.
An assessment confined to that practical benefit would nevertheless be incomplete, since sharing the work helps everyone feel included. In concrete terms, each guest
brings one dish and helps clear the table. This introduces a problem of perspective: whose convenience supplies the standard against which improvement is measured?
An apparently neutral procedure may privilege the preferences of its designer. Attentiveness to others makes that asymmetry visible and creates grounds for revision.
What emerges is a qualified defence of planning, rather than a celebration of either control or spontaneity. Arrangements can sustain an experience without exhausting its
meaning. Their authority should remain answerable to the people and circumstances they affect; otherwise, a means of making life more habitable risks becoming the
criterion to which life must conform.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example. Conclude by connecting the two
reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an experience of your own.
Explain the meaning before looking at the model answer. What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
